verdict.rationale: Harbor Compliance publishes a public, keyless OpenAPI document (probe-confirmed HTTP 200) for its v3 API. Server-to-server OAuth client-credentials auth is documented, along with refresh-token handling, secret rotation, rate-limit headers with Retry-After guidance, and Idempotency-Key support for safe retries. Together these give a programmatic consumer a solid way to drive the product. The main caveat is that create, update and delete require capabilities Harbor must explicitly grant per account, so write access is not self-serve. The probe also notes registered-agent endpoint markers were absent, leaving coverage of core surfaces unclear. missing for 10: self-serve write access without manual vendor grant, evidence of endpoint coverage across core product surfaces (entities, licenses, tax, annual reports), independent or hands-on corroboration of API use.
